electron.title: Electron
electron.summary: Bundles Chromium and Node.js with the app. Backend code is TypeScript running on Node, so any npm package works. Built with Electron Forge and Vite.
chooseWhen: The app needs Node libraries, native Node modules, a background process, a local database or peer-to-peer networking
The interface must render identically on every operating system
The team works in TypeScript end to end and does not want a Rust backend
avoidWhen: Installer size or memory use is a stated requirement (expect roughly a 100 MB floor)
The same codebase must also ship to iOS or Android

native.title: Native interface
native.summary: The window shows the bundled React + Vite interface. Works offline. Use when there is no hosted web app to reuse.

remote.title: Hosted web app
remote.summary: The window loads a web app you already host (for example Next.js with its server features). Needs a network connection.

exported.title: Bundled static export
exported.summary: Ships a static web build (for example `next build` with output: 'export') inside the app and serves it from a private app:// scheme. Works offline; server features are lost.

tauri.title: Tauri 2
tauri.summary: Uses the operating system's own web view and a compiled Rust backend. Small installers and low memory; backend code is Rust and every capability must be granted explicitly.
chooseWhen: The app is a thin client over a remote API or does most work in the interface
Installer size or memory use is a stated requirement
The team is willing to write backend logic in Rust, or iOS/Android from the same code is a real goal
avoidWhen: The backend must reuse Node libraries (they cannot run in Tauri without a sidecar process)
The interface depends on Chromium-only behavior (each OS renders with a different engine)

native.title: Native interface
native.summary: The window shows the bundled React + Vite interface embedded in the binary. Works offline.

remote.title: Hosted web app
remote.summary: The window loads a web app you already host. The hosted site gets no access to native commands unless its origin is granted in a capability file.

modules.title: Local database (SQLite)
modules.summary: Structured app data in a SQLite file in the user-data folder, with ordered migrations and an example notes repository.

modules.title: Secure storage
modules.summary: Encrypted storage for tokens and credentials using the operating system key store. The interface can save but never read back a secret.

modules.title: Sign-in (OpenID Connect + PKCE)
modules.summary: Sign-in through the system browser with PKCE; the provider redirects to <scheme>://auth/callback. Works with any OpenID Connect provider (Auth0, Okta, Entra ID, Keycloak, Cognito, Supabase, Google...).

issuer.description: OpenID Connect issuer URL, e.g. https://your-tenant.us.auth0.com

clientId.description: Client id of a public (native/SPA) application at the provider, with no client secret

scopes.description: Space- or comma-separated scopes (default: openid profile email offline_access)

audience.description: API audience, for providers that need one (Auth0)

manualSteps: At the identity provider, create a public/native application and add <scheme>://auth/callback as an allowed redirect URI (the scheme comes from the plan).
Linux: the deep link is registered when the .deb is installed; during development, test sign-in on Windows/macOS or with an installed build.

modules.title: Automatic updates
modules.summary: Checks for and installs new versions. Electron: GitHub releases of a public repository or any static file host. Tauri: signed update manifests from any URL.

source.description: Electron only: github (public repository) or static (any file host)

baseUrl.description: Electron static source: base URL where make output is uploaded

pubkey.description: Tauri: public key printed by `bun run tauri signer generate`

manualSteps: Electron github source: set repository in the plan, make the repository public, and publish with `bun run publish`.
Electron static source: upload `out/make` contents to <baseUrl>/<platform>/<arch>/ for each release.
Tauri: run `bun run tauri signer generate -w ~/.tauri/app.key`, put the public key in moduleOptions.auto-update.pubkey, and set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY (and _PASSWORD) when building releases.

modules.title: File access
modules.summary: Native open/save dialogs and reading or writing the files the user picked. Nothing outside the user's choices is reachable from the interface.

modules.title: Tray and background work
modules.summary: Tray icon, start at login, and work that continues when the window is closed (Electron: a utilityProcess worker; Tauri: an async Rust task).

modules.title: Crash reporting (Sentry)
modules.summary: Sends errors and native crashes from every process to a Sentry project.

dsn.description: Sentry project DSN (reporting stays off until set)

manualSteps: Upload source maps for readable stack traces (Sentry's Vite plugin) when you set up release builds.

modules.title: Prisma ORM instead of the built-in SQLite layer
modules.summary: For apps whose schema already lives in Prisma on a server. Not generated automatically because it adds a code-generation step and, with the better-sqlite3 adapter, a native module that must be rebuilt for Electron.
manualSteps: bun add @prisma/client @prisma/adapter-better-sqlite3 better-sqlite3 && bun add -d prisma
Add `"better-sqlite3"` to trustedDependencies in package.json and keep AutoUnpackNativesPlugin in forge.config.ts (already present).
Create prisma/schema.prisma with provider = "sqlite"; run `bunx prisma generate` before `bun run dev` and in CI.
Create the client only in the main process with new PrismaClient({ adapter: new PrismaBetterSqlite3({ url: `file:${path.join(app.getPath('userData'), 'app.db')}` }) }).
Ship migrations by running `prisma migrate diff` to SQL and applying them at start-up (the migration engine is not bundled), or ship a pre-migrated database file and copy it to userData on first run.
Electron Forge rebuilds better-sqlite3 for Electron during `bun run dev` and `bun run package`; verify with `bun run test:e2e`.

modules.title: Peer-to-peer transport
modules.summary: Direct device-to-device connections. Chosen per product, so it is documented rather than generated.
manualSteps: Pick the transport first: iroh (QUIC with relay fallback; Rust-first, strongest NAT traversal), libp2p (cross-language, modular), Hyperswarm (JavaScript DHT + hole punching), or WebRTC data channels (needs a signalling server).
Electron: run the transport in a utilityProcess worker (add the background module and put it in src/main/workers/).
Tauri: use the Rust crate directly (iroh, libp2p, quinn) in a tokio task started from setup(), and stream progress to the interface with a Channel.
Never put key material in a QR code; use a short-lived pairing token.

vite.title: React + Vite
vite.summary: A single-page React app built by Vite with TanStack Router (hash routes). The default; fastest builds and the simplest setup.

nextjs.title: Next.js (static export)
nextjs.summary: A Next.js App Router project exported to static files at build time (output: "export"). Use when the team already works in Next.js or wants its file-based routing. Server features (server actions, route handlers, middleware, image optimization, incremental regeneration) do not exist in a desktop app.

scripts.test:e2e: bun run build:web && electron-forge package && playwright test

shadcn.title: shadcn/ui
shadcn.summary: Accessible components copied into the app (Radix primitives styled with Tailwind CSS). Desktop-style by default and fully restylable. The default.

konsta.title: Konsta UI
konsta.summary: Tailwind CSS components that reproduce native iOS and Material Design (Android) look and behaviour: navigation bars, tab bars, lists, sheets, toggles. Use for an app-store look, especially with Tauri's Android/iOS targets. Module panels keep their shadcn/ui components.
